title: 55-Inch 4K TV in Vietnam: New and Used Prices, Checks
description: New and used 55-inch 4K TV prices in Ho Chi Minh City in November 2026, real sizes for your shelf, how to test a used TV, and when the warranty still applies.
h1: Buying a 55-inch 4K TV in Ho Chi Minh City: prices new and used, sizes, and the checks to make before you pay
intro: Before you buy a 55-inch 4K TV in Vietnam, measure your space (the set is about 123 cm wide), compare new and used prices, then check the serial number, invoice and screen. A genuine Samsung TV carries a 24-month manufacturer's warranty. Used sets cost far less, but usually come with only a short shop warranty.
keyPoints: According to CellphoneS, on 24 November 2026 new 55-inch 4K TVs were listed from {{vnd:7790000}} (TCL 55P638) to {{vnd:26990000}} (LG OLED 55C5PSA).
Used 55-inch TVs listed on Chợ Tốt in the District 7 area on 24 November 2026 were priced {{vnd:2790000-6800000}}, most showing a two-month shop warranty.
A 55-inch TV body is about 122.6–123.5 cm wide and 70–72 cm tall wall-mounted, according to Điện Máy Xanh; it recommends sitting 2.7–4 m from the screen.
Samsung Vietnam's warranty policy refuses cover for a TV with a missing serial number or no valid proof of purchase, so ask a seller for the original invoice.
Switch a used TV on and test plain white and black screens, every HDMI port and the remote before paying. Photos in a listing hide dead pixels and backlight bleed.

sections.title: How much does a new 55-inch 4K TV cost in Vietnam?

blocks.text: New 55-inch 4K TVs at the big electronics chains run from about {{vnd:7790000}} to {{vnd:26990000}}, and the panel type drives most of the difference. These are the starting prices CellphoneS listed on 24 November 2026; promotional prices at Vietnamese chains change week to week.

blocks.caption: Selected new 55-inch 4K TVs, starting prices listed by CellphoneS on 24 November 2026

blocks.text: Other chains price the same segment differently. According to FPT Shop, on 24 November 2026 the Samsung UA55DU8000 (4K, 60 Hz) was offered at {{vnd:8990000}}, a {{vnd:6400000}} discount on its {{vnd:15390000}} list price, valid until 30 November and marked as a display unit. The page lists a **24-month genuine-product warranty** but does not say whether display units get it. Because the gap between list and sale price is often this wide, compare the price you would actually pay today, not the crossed-out one.
Which panel type is worth paying for?

On a tight budget, standard LED/UHD and entry QLED sets are the cheapest: in the CellphoneS list above they sit around {{vnd:7790000-10390000}}. QNED, Mini LED and Neo QLED sets form the middle tier, roughly {{vnd:12490000-16990000}} on the same page, and OLED costs much more. If you play on a console, check the refresh rate: most entry models are 60 Hz, while some TCL Mini LED models put 144 Hz in the product name.

sections.title: How much is a used 55-inch TV in Ho Chi Minh City?

blocks.text: A used 55-inch 4K TV in Ho Chi Minh City costs anywhere from about a third of the cheapest new set to almost as much. On 24 November 2026, Chợ Tốt listings in the District 7 area ran from {{vnd:2790000}} to {{vnd:6800000}}, leaving aside a set sold as broken. On the same day the cheapest new 55-inch 4K TV at CellphoneS was {{vnd:7790000}}, so the dearest used listing was only {{vnd:990000}} cheaper than a new set. Returned stock sold by a chain costs more than a private listing but comes with a clearer history.

blocks.caption: Used 55-inch TV prices: Chợ Tốt listings in the District 7 area read on 24 November 2026, and FPT Shop's used-goods page rechecked on 25 November 2026
rows: FPT Shop, returned stock (units listed in Ho Chi Minh City)
Not stated on the product page

blocks.text: FPT Shop's page for the returned Samsung UA55DU7700, read on 25 November 2026, gives the price and the provinces where units are held but does not state a warranty period for these units; it links only to FPT Shop's general warranty policy and warranty lookup. Ask FPT Shop what warranty a specific unit carries before you buy it.

Many listings do not give the year. Before comparing prices, ask the seller for the full model number (for example UA55DU7700 or 55UQ7550). With it you can look up the model year and compare it with the new price of the same line. A used set only a few million đồng cheaper than the cheapest new 55-inch model is rarely a good deal.
Listings are in Vietnamese. **Bảo hành** means warranty, **hóa đơn** means invoice, **giao lắp** means delivery and installation, and **hỏng màn hình** means the screen is broken.

blocks.title: New ward names
blocks.text: Since 1 July 2025, official addresses no longer use districts, so listings now give new ward names: in the old District 7 area you will see Phú Thuận or Tân Mỹ. Ask the seller for the exact address before you go to see a TV. For the area itself, see [District 7, Ho Chi Minh City](/guides/district-7-ho-chi-minh-city).

To sell your own TV or find one someone else has listed, use [the Electronics category on eno.vn](/c/electronics). If you are meeting a stranger to see an item, read [eno.vn's safety advice](/safety) first.

sections.title: Will a 55-inch TV fit your room?

blocks.text: A 55-inch TV has a screen diagonal of about 139.7 cm and a body about 122.6–123.5 cm wide, depending on the brand. It stands about 70–72 cm tall wall-mounted and about 75–78 cm on its stand. These are Điện Máy Xanh's figures, updated 6 October 2025, and it notes that individual models can differ by 1–2 cm.

blocks.caption: 55-inch TV dimensions by brand (width × height × depth), according to Điện Máy Xanh, updated 6 October 2025

blocks.text: Measure the **depth of your TV unit**, not just its width. The Sony and TCL stands are more than 33 cm deep, so a narrow shelf in a rented flat may not hold them. Điện Máy Xanh recommends sitting 2.7–4 m from a 55-inch screen and calls the size suited to a room of about 15–20 m². If that sounds too big, see [42-inch TV dimensions](/guides/42-inch-tv-dimensions).
What should you check about the stand on a used TV?

Ask whether the original stand or a wall bracket comes with the set. Used TVs are often sold without the stand, and a replacement has to match the model. If you rent, ask your landlord before drilling a wall to mount the TV; [renting an apartment in Vietnam](/renting-an-apartment-vietnam-foreigner) covers what to agree with them.

sections.title: How to check a used 55-inch TV before you pay

blocks.text: Watch the TV running for at least 15–20 minutes, match the serial numbers and try every port. Screen and backlight faults only show once the set has been on for a while with a plain single-colour image, and listing photos cannot show them.

items.title: Get the model and serial number before you go
items.text: The model number tells you the year and panel type; the serial number is what the warranty is checked against. Samsung Vietnam's product registration page asks for the serial number on the product itself, not the one printed on the box.

items.title: Match the sticker to the menu
items.text: Open Settings and the device information or About screen, and compare the serial number with the sticker on the back. If the sticker is peeled, faded or does not match, think about walking away: Samsung's policy excludes sets whose original serial number is missing or unreadable.

items.title: Test plain white, black, red and blue screens
items.text: Play full-screen single-colour images from a USB stick or YouTube. Look for dead pixels, lines, bright patches at the corners (backlight bleed) and colour tints. On an OLED, look closely at a grey screen for a burnt-in logo.

items.title: Play a 4K HDR video
items.text: Stream a 4K video on YouTube or a built-in app to test the Wi-Fi, decoding and speakers. Stuttering, spontaneous restarts or lost sound point to a board fault.

items.title: Try every HDMI port, the USB ports and the remote
items.text: Bring a phone or laptop and an HDMI cable and plug into each port in turn. Press every button on the remote, including voice control if the listing advertises it.

items.title: Get paperwork when you pay
items.text: Ask for the original purchase invoice if the seller has it, and a receipt showing the model, serial number, price and the seller's warranty period. If the seller agrees, pay once the TV is delivered and has worked again in your home.

blocks.title: The most common mistake
blocks.text: Buyers watch a few minutes of a bright, colourful demo video in the shop. That hides dead pixels and backlight bleed. Always test plain single-colour screens, especially black in a dark room.

sections.title: Does a second-hand TV still have the manufacturer's warranty?

blocks.text: It may, if it is still within the period and you can prove where it was bought. According to Samsung Vietnam's warranty policy, read on 24 November 2026, Samsung TVs carry 24 months' warranty, Full HD TVs 12 months and Micro LED TVs 60 months.

Samsung counts the warranty from the day the customer first activates the product, or from the VAT invoice date if that cannot be established. The policy covers products **bought new** in their original packaging and does not say whether a later buyer inherits the cover. If warranty is your reason for choosing a set, call Samsung's support line with the serial number and ask before you buy.
When is a TV definitely not covered?

items: When you **cannot show valid proof of purchase**.
When the original manufacturer's serial number is missing or unreadable.
Damage from drops, knocks, cracks, water or other liquids, unauthorised repairs or misuse.
Accessories not supplied with the product, such as separate cables and memory cards.

blocks.text: Dead pixels have their own test. Samsung's policy treats a screen as faulty when it shows a white dot, two black dots less than 5 mm apart, or five or more scattered black dots. Once the manufacturer's warranty has run out, only the seller's warranty is left; on the District 7 area listings of 24 November 2026 that was usually two months.

For other brands (LG, Sony, TCL, Xiaomi), each manufacturer sets its own warranty period and conditions. Check the brand's official support page or call its support line rather than relying on the seller.

sections.title: What this guide does not cover

items: Picture-quality reviews of individual models: this guide compares listed prices, panel types and sizes only. See the sets side by side in a shop.
Prices in Hanoi and other provinces: the used-TV figures here come from the District 7 area of Ho Chi Minh City.

Kitting out the rest of a flat: see [furnishing a home in Vietnam](/furnishing-a-home-in-vietnam) and [second-hand furniture in Ho Chi Minh City](/secondhand-furniture-ho-chi-minh-city). Selling a TV before you leave: see [selling up before you leave Vietnam](/selling-up-before-you-leave-vietnam).

faqs.q: How much is a 55-inch 4K TV in Vietnam?
faqs.a: According to CellphoneS on 24 November 2026, new 55-inch 4K TVs in Vietnam ranged from the TCL 55P638 at the cheapest to the LG OLED 55C5PSA at the top, with QLED, QNED and Mini LED models in between. The exact price of each model is in the price table in this guide. Chain promotions change weekly, so compare the sale price on the day rather than the list price.

faqs.q: How wide is a 55-inch TV in cm?
faqs.a: A 55-inch TV has a screen diagonal of about 139.7 cm and a body about 122.6 to 123.5 cm wide, depending on the brand. It stands about 70 to 72 cm tall wall-mounted and 75 to 78 cm on its stand, according to Điện Máy Xanh figures updated on 6 October 2025. Some stands are more than 33 cm deep, so measure the depth of your TV unit as well.

faqs.q: How far should you sit from a 55-inch TV?
faqs.a: Điện Máy Xanh recommends sitting 2.7 to 4 metres from a 55-inch TV and says the size suits a room of about 15 to 20 square metres. Measure from your usual seat to where the TV will go before buying. The centre of the screen should be roughly at eye level when you are seated, so long viewing does not strain your neck.

faqs.q: Is it worth buying a used 55-inch TV in Ho Chi Minh City?
faqs.a: A used 55-inch TV in Ho Chi Minh City is worth buying when it is clearly cheaper than the cheapest new set of the same size, still has its original serial number, and passes a test of the screen, HDMI ports and remote. On 24 November 2026, most used 55-inch TV listings in the District 7 area showed only a two-month shop warranty, far shorter than a new set's manufacturer warranty.

faqs.q: How do I check a used TV for dead pixels?
faqs.a: To check a used TV for dead pixels, play full-screen single-colour images (white, black, red, blue) from a USB stick or YouTube and look closely at each part of the screen. A dark dot on white or a bright dot on black is a faulty pixel. Test in a dark room so you can also see backlight bleed at the corners of the screen.

faqs.q: Does a second-hand Samsung TV keep its warranty in Vietnam?
faqs.a: Samsung TVs in Vietnam carry a 24-month warranty counted from first activation or the VAT invoice date. Samsung Vietnam's policy excludes sets with a missing serial number or no proof of purchase, and does not say whether a later buyer inherits the cover. Ask the seller for the original invoice and call Samsung's support line with the serial number before buying a second-hand Samsung TV.

faqs.q: Where is the serial number on a Samsung TV?
faqs.a: The serial number on a Samsung TV is printed on the sticker on the back of the set and also appears in the device information screen in the settings. Samsung Vietnam asks for the serial number on the product itself, not the one on the box, when you register or check warranty. When buying a used Samsung TV, compare the two numbers: a peeled or mismatched sticker is a warning sign.
